---
title: "Before project closure and handover"
---

**Pause point:** Before access ends, people leave, accounts close, records are archived or responsibility transfers.

**Prevents:** Losing the research record, leaving obligations without an owner, retaining data unlawfully, or handing over files that another person cannot understand or recover.

**Use:** Do-confirm.

## Critical checks

- [ ] Final research records have approved, documented locations rather than depending on one person's device or account.
- [ ] Data and records marked for disposal can be destroyed lawfully without removing material that must be retained.
- [ ] Ownership, custody, access, retention, sharing, embargo and confidentiality obligations have been reconciled.
- [ ] Data, code, software dependencies, metadata and file structure are sufficient for the authorised future use.
- [ ] Publications, persistent identifiers, approvals, protocols, decisions, deviations and final outputs are linked to the same record.
- [ ] Open actions, incidents, complaints, agreements, contracts and reporting obligations are resolved or transferred to a named owner.
- [ ] Personal access can be removed without disabling shared services, automation, repositories or recovery routes.
- [ ] The receiving person has opened the key files, located the critical evidence and tested the documented recovery or reproduction steps.
- [ ] Known limitations, incomplete work and conditions on reuse are stated plainly.
- [ ] The handover has a named recipient, acknowledgement, date and future owner.

## Stop condition

Do not close or hand over while the only recoverable copy is in personal storage, key files cannot be opened, or legal, ethical, contractual or reporting obligations have no owner.

## Evidence to retain

Keep the closure decision, archive manifest, access record, disposal evidence, handover note, recipient acknowledgement, outstanding-obligation register and final integrity check.

::: {.callout-warning title="Check locally"}
Retention, disposal, ownership, repository, departure and account-closure rules vary by institution, funder, agreement, jurisdiction and data type.
:::
